name: Chain of Torah Tradition (Mesorah)
notes: The transmission of Torah from Sinai through generations: Moses to Joshua to elders to prophets to Men of Great Assembly, and onward. A central theme of Avot ch. 1.

name: Torah Study for Its Own Sake (Torah Lishmah)
notes: The ideal of studying Torah intrinsically, not for reward or status; contrasted with using Torah as a spade (Avot 4:5, 6:1).

name: Fence Around the Torah (Seyag laTorah)
notes: The principle of erecting protective enactments around Torah law to prevent transgression; mentioned in Avot 1:1, 3:13.

name: Torah Combined with Worldly Occupation (Torah im Derech Eretz)
notes: The value and necessity of combining Torah study with a livelihood; discussed in Avot 2:2.

name: Dispute for the Sake of Heaven (Machloket leShem Shamayim)
notes: Distinction between disputes conducted for the sake of heaven (Hillel and Shammai) vs. those not (Korach); Avot 5:17.

name: Ten Utterances of Creation (Asarah Maamarot)
notes: The world was created with ten divine utterances; the theological significance of this for reward and punishment (Avot 5:1).

name: Causing the Multitudes to Sin or to be Righteous
hebrew: מחטיא את הרבים / מזכה את הרבים
notes: One who causes the public to sin cannot repent; one who causes the public to be righteous is credited with their righteousness (Avot 5:18).

name: This World as Vestibule to the World to Come
notes: The metaphor of this world as a vestibule (prozdor) preparing for the banquet hall of the World to Come (Avot 4:16).

name: Reward for a Commandment is a Commandment (Mitzvah Goreret Mitzvah)
notes: One mitzvah leads to another mitzvah, and one transgression leads to another transgression (Avot 4:2).

name: Prayer for the Welfare of the Government
notes: The obligation to pray for governmental stability, since without it people would devour one another (Avot 3:2).

name: Shekhinah Among Torah Learners
notes: Divine presence rests among those studying Torah, whether ten, five, three, two, or even one (Avot 3:2, 3:6).

name: Serving God Without Expectation of Reward
hebrew: עבודה שלא על מנת לקבל פרס
notes: The ideal of serving God like servants who do not expect reward, but purely out of reverence (Avot 1:3).

name: Do Not Separate from the Community
notes: The principle that one should not separate oneself from the communal life (Avot 2:4).

name: Divine Foreknowledge and Human Free Will
notes: The paradox that everything is foreseen yet freedom of choice is granted; world judged by preponderance of deeds (Avot 3:15).

name: Who is Wise, Mighty, Rich, Honored (Ben Zoma)
hebrew: איזהו חכם איזהו גיבור איזהו עשיר איזהו מכובד
notes: Ben Zoma's redefinition of wisdom, strength, wealth, and honor in ethical and spiritual terms (Avot 4:1). Widely quoted throughout Talmudic literature.

name: Quoting a Teaching in the Name of Its Author
notes: The obligation to cite one's source when transmitting a teaching; doing so brings redemption to the world (Avot 6:6).
